# Spiritual Translation: The Primordial Natures

---

**¶2.** What the inmost nature of [GAP-1] the Divine Itself is — no finite understanding could comprehend or disclose [GAP-2] how its infinite being subsists [GAP-3] from eternity to eternity — all [GAP-4] perceptions and [GAP-5] cognitions disclose [GAP-6] only [GAP-7] what is eternal [GAP-8] in its infinitely [GAP-9] surpassing nature; and yet the [GAP-10] finite mind tends [GAP-11] to grasp the origin of what is eternal and its consummation [GAP-12], yet cannot circumscribe it.

---

**¶3.** The realm of spiritual death [GAP-13] — the inmost quality of its essential nature [GAP-14], which subsists [GAP-15] perpetually and without end [GAP-16] in [GAP-17] mutual opposition with one another.

---

**¶4.** As for the eternity of [GAP-18] those infernal states which subsist from before all remembrance, no finite intelligence is able to [GAP-19] comprehend how they exist. For no other power was ever made manifest to them by which they might articulate or recount their own origin, how they came to be. However, from the time when evil stirred itself from within and rose up against Wisdom [GAP-20], desiring that it might invade and rule over the realm of spiritual life.

---

**¶5.** The Divine Human in His first proceeding came forth against it and opposed it, [GAP-21] separating it from heaven, the dwelling-place of the living. He held it at bay. From that time, when wisdom was commingled with [GAP-22] falsity, and spiritual life with spiritual death,

---

**¶6.** [GAP-23] after evil stirred itself in its own essential nature, its in[GAP-24]tention and deliberation arose within its own domain. It [GAP-25] pervaded the entire realm of falsity in its [GAP-26] desperate craving for the [GAP-27] quality of wisdom perceived in the abyss. For [GAP-27] its essential nature within [GAP-28] itself was such that [GAP-29] all the infernal powers [GAP-30] reckoned [GAP-30] upon its dominion [GAP-31]. This primordial quality of evil [GAP-32] was of such a character that its external form was hardened [GAP-33] beyond even the most confirmed falsity, the Adamantine resistance [GAP-34], surpassing every [GAP-35] opposing force as it subsists throughout the whole of the created order.

---

**¶7.** [GAP-36] Of spiritual death [GAP-37] arose that envy which [GAP-38] pervaded the realm of [GAP-39] falsity and evil, a deliberate [GAP-40] intention toward wickedness [GAP-41], for as it [GAP-42] inflicted its injuries [GAP-43] against the realm of spiritual life [GAP-44].

---

**¶8.** Then the Divine Human will hasten [GAP-45] from the realm [GAP-46] of falsity. Evil drew upon [GAP-47] his faculties and particular powers [GAP-48], and what is of the abyss is profound [GAP-49] within them.

---

**¶9.** [GAP-50] Every [GAP-51] infernal state proliferated. Evil spread itself throughout. It generated itself [GAP-52] into the five fundamental states of the infernal mind; which [GAP-53] are: obscurity of understanding, self-love, vain reasoning, falsity of doctrine, and utter spiritual blindness. [GAP-54] It brought forth perverted perceptions. It ascended [GAP-55] and it formed its own being in the [GAP-56] likeness of those perceptions; it generated its own nature through its propagation [GAP-57] in innumerable derivative forms, none resembling another; [GAP-58] in the repositories of its abyss, many [GAP-59] infernal affections and drives — [GAP-60] destroyers of good, interior falsities that devour truth, and evil desires of every kind. Evil was established and [GAP-61] confirmed and grew powerful [GAP-62] in the hideous forms assumed by those dwelling in falsity, [GAP-63] wholly devoid of light, and by the [GAP-64] violence of their impulse, by their wickedness and mutual hatred they consume [GAP-65] one another, as they exist in perpetual conflict with themselves.

---

**¶10.** Then the deliberation of the ruling love of self subdued its own mental realm and all its derivative powers. It perceived the essential quality of [GAP-66] divine wisdom and good from afar. It conspired to wage spiritual combat [GAP-67] against the celestial kingdom and the [GAP-68] Divine order that governs it.

---

**¶11.** However, He — the Divine Itself, the Father of Infinite [GAP-69] Being — perceived it, and [GAP-70] foreknew the intent of spiritual combat, to assault the [GAP-71] realm of divine wisdom [GAP-72]. Yet in the wisdom of His [GAP-73] providence [GAP-74], He disposed Himself against evil [GAP-75] and set the means of its opposition.

---

**¶12.** Indeed, at that time [GAP-76] the whole infernal host prepared to [GAP-77] assault the [GAP-78] Divine order.

---

**¶13.** [GAP-79] From its own [GAP-80] interior nature it poured forth [GAP-81] its qualities into the fundamental infernal states: into the obscurity of understanding, the self-love, the vain reasoning, the falsity of doctrine, and the utter spiritual blindness. It ascended from the [GAP-82] profoundest depths of hell, it being fixed and rooted in the perverted perceptions [GAP-83] arrayed against wisdom.

---

**¶14.** Also, at the time when evil generated itself from those perceptions, [GAP-84] it formed works of its own nature, while still remaining rooted in them. Then were summoned the five external truths — the divine principles proceeding from the Divine Human.

---

**¶15.** And at the time when evil generated its own nature from those works through its propagated offspring, these derivative evils descended into the natural mind and [GAP-85] drew sustaining power from the fundamental infernal states and were nourished by them. [GAP-86] Wickedness together with cruelty [GAP-87] concentrated in the ruling love of self, the chief of all infernal spirits. He subdued all his derivative realms and their powers; he gathered them all into himself as into one dominating will. He made himself ready for the spiritual combat; he set himself to war against the realm of divine wisdom, and the great Divine Governing Principle who dwells within it.

---

**¶16.** At that very moment the Divine Human drew near to His external truths, the divine principles that radiate forth with their own light. He communed with them, that He might entrust to them a [GAP-88] commission for combat; He [GAP-89] revealed to them and instructed them concerning everything that would befall [GAP-89] them. He assumed them into Himself. He arranged them [GAP-90] in proper order. He draped them one over another upon His own faculties [GAP-91], against the coming danger, as evil [GAP-92] rose against the elevated states of the celestial mind [GAP-93] with all its infernal powers [GAP-94] from the very beginning, its malice being immeasurable [GAP-95].

---

### Translator's Note

The five "elements" of Darkness — smoke, fire, wind, water, and darkness — correspond to five fundamental states of the infernal mind: *obscurity of understanding* (smoke), *self-love* (fire in the opposite sense), *vain reasoning and empty persuasion* (wind), *falsity of doctrine* (water in the opposite sense), and *utter spiritual blindness* (darkness proper). These are not physical substances but the constituent qualities of every evil, as it propagates itself through perverted perception into evil works.

The five "garments" of the First Man correspond to *external divine truths* — the successive coverings of wisdom by which the Divine Human engages with and overcomes evil. In Swedenborg's terms, these are the accommodated forms of divine truth through which the Lord fights in temptation on behalf of the human being.

The overall chapter describes the eternal separation of good and evil, the self-propagation of evil through perverted perceptions into destructive works, and the Divine preparation for spiritual combat — the Lord's assumption of successive truths as the means of redemption.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: What the essence of [the Light]—no person could recount or unveil [or say how it] exists [from ever for ever and ever]—all [minds] and [tongues] unveil [only] [its] eternity [and its] great [glory] again and the [senses] tend [toward] the beginning of eternity and the end [cannot] set that one down.
the land of Death [and also the] nature of the essence [of Death] which exists [from ever and for e]ver and ever [dwelling] in [strife] with one another.

As for the eternity of [the land of Darkness] which exists from ever, no person is able to [understand] how they exist. For no other power [is manifes]ted to them, in that it might speak or recount about their origin, how [they e]xist. However, from the time when it stirred itself and rose up against the Light [desiring that] it might come and rule over the land of the Living.

[The Fi]rst Man came forth against it and prevented it, [he kept] it apart from the house of the Living. He prevented it. From that time, when the Light was mixed with [the] Darkness, and Life [wi]th Death,

[and after it] stirred itself in its essence, its th[ought and counsel arose] in its own land. It [ ... ... ] the entire land of Darkness in its [desire for the sight] of Light in the abyss. For [its] essence in [i]t [ ... ... ] because a [ ... ] they reckoned [ ... ... ] on its side [ ... ] this first nature [of] it, because its body is made strong [and hard more] than the Adamant [above] every [power] as it exists [in the univer]se.
[Out] of Death [there arose that] envy, which [filled] the land of [Darkness, with consi]deration in [its] wickedness [ ... ] for as it [inflicted] the wounds [ ... ] against this land [of Light]
Then he will run [forth f]rom the land [of] Darkness. It drew [upon] his members [and it] is deep [and rooted] in them.

[ ... ] every [ ... ] It spread itself out. It generated itself [of the five dark elements]; which [are] smoke, fire, wind, water and Darkness. [From them it] sprouted trees. It came up [from the depth and] it formed its own self in the [trees] it generated its own self with its birth [in] numerous [emana]tions, not resembling each other; [in] the storehouses of its abyss, many [dark] creatures [and] destroyers and dragons and evil beasts. It was established and [rooted] and grew strong [and appeared] in the ugly forms of those in the Darkness [all] dark, and by the [their] impetuosity, by their wickedness and hatred they slaughter [and devour] each other as they war with one another.
Then the counsel of their ruler humbled its world and its powers. It sensed the essence of the [Light from afar] It conspired to wage a war [and a battle] with the exalted kingdom and the [Light]

However, he, the Father of Great[ness, he perceived it and] it also knew [the] war, to disturb the [land of] Light [yet] in the wisdom of his [great]-ness [and] he transformed himself against it [and sent his power] against it.
Indeed, at that time [ ... ... ... ] go against [the] God [ ... ]

[And fr]om its [essence] poured it out [and spread it] in the elements: in the smoke, the fire, the wind, the water and the Darkness. It came up from the [great] depth, it being set in the trees [that were arrayed] against it.
Also, at the time when it generated itself [and] it formed the fruits, it still being set in them. They summoned the five garments, the sons of the Fir[st] Man.

And at the time when it generated its own self [f]rom the fruits through its offspring, they fell upon the earth and [drew] strength from the elements and were nourished by them. [And all the] wickedness, together with cruelty [gathered] in the ruler, the leader of all the demons. He hum[bled] his worlds and his powers; he gathered them all into him. He made himself ready for the battle; he set himself to the war with that Light earth, and the great King who dwells in it.

At that very moment the First Man approached his garments, the gods [who sh]ine forth. He spoke with them, that he might entrust to them a [command] he [reve]aled to them and taught them about everything that [would come upon] them. He assumed them. He arranged them [upon himself] He draped them over one another upon his limbs [against the coming] danger, it [rose up against] the heights of the earth [ ... ... ] with all its powers [from the beg]inning, it being immeasurable [ ... ... ]

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading identifies this as "the Divine Itself," which in the Kephalaia's natural-plane register is always "the Light" — the supreme divine principle.

The editor's reading fits the spiritual sense of expressing the incomprehensibility of the Divine: "recount or unveil or say how it exists" parallels "comprehend or disclose how its infinite being subsists."

fills.explanation: Standard Coptic Manichaean formula for eternal existence ("from eternity to eternity"), with "for ever" being the partially legible portion of the gap.
The spiritual reading says "perceptions"; in the Kephalaia, "minds" is the standard term for the inner perceptive faculty, commonly paired with "tongues" as the expressive faculty.

The spiritual reading says "cognitions" (expressive knowledge); "tongues" is the standard Kephalaia counterpart to "minds," forming the common pair "minds and tongues" for faculties that perceive and articulate.
The spiritual reading says "disclose only what is eternal" — the limiting word "only" emphasizes that finite faculties can reveal merely a portion of the infinite.
The spiritual reading says "what is eternal" referring to the Light's eternity; "its" connects to "eternity" making "its eternity" — the eternity belonging to the Light.

The spiritual reading says "in its infinitely surpassing nature"; "and its" connects "eternity" to "great [glory]," yielding "unveil only its eternity and its great glory" — the two aspects of the Divine that finite faculties can partially disclose.

The spiritual reading says "infinitely surpassing nature"; "great glory" is one of the most common collocations in the Kephalaia for the Divine's transcendent splendor, completing "its eternity and its great glory."
The spiritual reading says "the finite mind"; in Kephalaia register, "senses" denotes the limited faculties that attempt to grasp what is infinite, complementing "minds" used earlier.
The spiritual reading says "tends to grasp the origin"; "toward" provides the directional sense of the senses striving toward comprehension of eternity's beginning.
The spiritual reading says "yet cannot circumscribe it"; "cannot set that one down" means cannot define or delimit the Divine — expressing the impossibility of finite comprehension of infinity.

The spiritual reading shows an appositive connection between "the realm of spiritual death" and "the inmost quality of its essential nature"; "and also the" bridges these as paired descriptions of the same reality.
The spiritual reading says "its essential nature" referring back to Death; "of Death" specifies the possessor — "the nature of the essence of Death, which exists from ever and for ever and ever."
Standard Kephalaia formula for perpetual existence; the fill completes "from ever and for ever and ever," a formulaic expression for eternity in both directions.

The spiritual reading says the two natures subsist "in mutual opposition"; "dwelling" provides the participial bridge between eternal duration and the mode of existence — "for ever and ever, dwelling in strife with one another."
The spiritual reading says "mutual opposition"; in the Kephalaia's natural-plane register, "strife" denotes the perpetual conflict between the two natures existing in opposition with one another.
The spiritual reading says "those infernal states"; this paragraph discusses the incomprehensible eternity of evil, and "the land of Darkness" is the Kephalaia's standard term for the infernal realm.
The spiritual reading says "comprehend"; the editor's "understand" is a precise natural-plane synonym and fits the context of finite inability to comprehend the eternal origin of evil.
The spiritual reading says "desiring that it might invade and rule"; this supplies the motive clause connecting the Darkness's rising against the Light to its intention to rule.
The editor's reading fits the spiritual sense of "separating it from heaven"; "he kept it apart from the house of the Living" accurately describes the First Man's protective act of separation.
The definite article before "Darkness" is standard Kephalaia usage when referring to the cosmic principle of Darkness as a named entity.
The spiritual reading says "after evil stirred itself"; the gap begins a new paragraph continuing the temporal narrative from ¶5's "from that time," with "and after it" providing the transition.

The word beginning "th-" is "thought"; the spiritual reading says "intention and deliberation arose within its own domain" — "thought and counsel" is the standard Kephalaia pair for inner intention and deliberation.

The spiritual reading says "desperate craving for the quality of wisdom perceived in the abyss"; in Manichaean cosmogony the Darkness perceived and desired the Light — "in its desire for the sight of Light in the abyss" describes this craving.
The spiritual reading says "its essential nature within itself"; the possessive "its" refers back to Darkness, indicating the essence belonging to it.

The spiritual reading says "this primordial quality of evil"; the preposition "of" connects "this first nature" to "it" (Darkness), indicating possession — "this first nature of it, because its body is made strong."

The spiritual reading says "hardened beyond even the most confirmed falsity"; "and hard more than the Adamant" adds the quality of hardness to strength, with the Adamant as the superlative comparison.
The spiritual reading says "surpassing every opposing force"; "above" expresses superlative comparison in the Kephalaia register — harder than Adamant, above every other power.
The spiritual reading says "every opposing force"; in the Kephalaia, "power" is the standard term for force or might, completing "above every power as it exists in the universe."
The spiritual reading says "Of spiritual death arose that envy"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, "Out of Death" introduces the origination of envy from within the nature of Death.
The spiritual reading says "arose that envy"; "there arose that" is the standard Kephalaia construction for the emergence of a quality from a primordial source.
The spiritual reading says "pervaded the realm"; "filled" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane verb for something pervading or saturating an entire domain.

The partially legible "Darkness" begins the gap and "consi" + "deration" forms "consideration"; the spiritual reading says "a deliberate consideration" — connecting the realm of Darkness to its deliberate intent.
The spiritual reading says "intention toward wickedness"; "its" makes "consideration in its wickedness" — the deliberate intention directed toward evil's own wickedness.
The spiritual reading says "inflicted its injuries"; "inflicted" is the natural-plane verb completing "for as it inflicted the wounds against this land."

The spiritual reading says "against the realm of spiritual life"; in the Kephalaia, the target of Darkness's assault is always "the land of Light" — "against this land of Light" identifies what is under attack.
The spiritual reading says "hasten from the realm"; "forth" + "f" + "rom" = "forth from" — "he will run forth from the land" describes the Divine Human hastening out against evil.
The preposition "of" completes "from the land of Darkness" — the standard Kephalaia construction for the realm of evil.
The spiritual reading says "drew upon his faculties"; "upon" completes "It drew upon his members" — Darkness drawing upon the First Man's constituent powers.

The spiritual reading says "and what is of the abyss is profound"; "and it" bridges the two clauses — "It drew upon his members, and it is deep in them" — connecting the drawing upon faculties to the depth of the abyss within them.

The spiritual reading says "what is of the abyss is profound within them"; "deep and rooted" expresses how the abyssal quality became fixed within the First Man's members — the same pairing of depth and rootedness used earlier in the chapter for evil's establishment.

The editor's reading correctly identifies the five dark elements as the products of evil's self-generation; "of" indicates composition — evil generated itself consisting of these five fundamental infernal qualities.
The copula "are" introduces the enumeration of the five dark elements: smoke, fire, wind, water, and Darkness.

The spiritual reading says "It brought forth perverted perceptions"; "From them" refers back to the five dark elements just enumerated — the Darkness brought forth trees (perverted perceptions) from these elemental qualities.

The spiritual reading says "It ascended and it formed"; "from the depth" parallels ¶13's "from the great depth" — the Darkness came up from the depth and formed itself, a standard Kephalaia description of evil's ascent from its abyss.

The spiritual reading says "in the likeness of those perceptions"; in the Kephalaia, "trees" corresponds to perverted perceptions — the natural-plane image for evil's self-forming through distorted cognition.
The editor's "in" correctly introduces the description of the numerous emanations: "in numerous emanations, not resembling each other."
The editor's "in" correctly introduces the location of the dark creatures: "in the storehouses of its abyss" — the repositories of evil's deepest nature.
The editor's "dark" correctly qualifies the creatures as belonging to the infernal realm; "dark creatures" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane term for infernal affections and drives.
The conjunction "and" connects the general category "dark creatures" to the specific enumeration "destroyers and dragons and evil beasts" in the Kephalaia's characteristic listing style.
The spiritual reading says "confirmed"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, "rooted" expresses the confirming or establishing of evil — it was established and rooted and grew strong.

The spiritual reading describes evil growing powerful and manifesting in hideous forms; "and appeared" adds the final step in the progression — established, rooted, grew strong, and appeared in the ugly forms of those in Darkness.
The spiritual reading says "wholly devoid of light"; "all dark" intensifies the description — everything in the Darkness is entirely dark, expressing complete absence of wisdom.
The spiritual reading says "violence of their impulse"; "their" parallels "by their wickedness and hatred" in the next clause, maintaining the consistent attribution to the dark creatures.
The spiritual reading says "they consume one another"; "slaughter and devour" is a standard hendiadys in Manichaean descriptions of the dark creatures' mutual destruction within the infernal realm.
The spiritual reading says "divine wisdom and good from afar"; in Manichaean cosmogony, the ruler of Darkness perceives the Light from a distance, which provokes its desire to wage war.
The spiritual reading says "to wage spiritual combat"; "war and battle" is a standard Kephalaia hendiadys for military conflict, completing "to wage a war and a battle with the exalted kingdom."
The spiritual reading says "the Divine order that governs it"; in the Kephalaia, "the Light" is the governing divine principle, completing "the exalted kingdom and the Light."

Completes "Greatness" and continues with the Father's perception of evil's intent; the spiritual reading says "the Father of Infinite Being perceived it, and foreknew" — mapping to "he perceived it and it also knew."
The spiritual reading says "foreknew the intent of spiritual combat"; "the" makes "it also knew the war" — the Father's foreknowledge of the coming conflict.
The editor's reading is confirmed; "land of Light" is the standard Kephalaia term for the divine realm, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "realm of divine wisdom."
The spiritual reading shows a contrast: evil intends to disturb the land of Light, "Yet in the wisdom of His providence" the Father responds — "yet" provides the adversative transition.
The spiritual reading says "providence"; in the Kephalaia, "greatness" is the primary divine attribute of the Father of Greatness — "wisdom of his greatness" expresses divine providential governance.
The conjunction "and" connects the description of the Father's wisdom to his responsive action: "in the wisdom of his greatness, and he transformed himself against it."

The spiritual reading says "and set the means of its opposition"; in the Kephalaia, the Father of Greatness sends forth a divine power against evil — "he transformed himself against it and sent his power against it."
In Coptic Manichaean usage, "God" regularly takes the definite article (ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ); "go against the God" follows standard Kephalaia grammar for referring to the supreme deity.

The paragraph begins with a temporal-descriptive phrase; "And fr" + "om" = "And from" — "And from its essence poured it out," initiating the description of evil pouring its qualities into the elements.
The spiritual reading says "from its own interior nature"; "essence" is the Kephalaia's term for the inmost nature of a being — evil poured forth from its own essence.

The spiritual reading says "poured forth its qualities into the fundamental infernal states"; "poured it out and spread it in the elements" pairs the act of outpouring with distribution across the five dark elements.
The editor's "great" is confirmed; "great depth" corresponds to the spiritual reading's "profoundest depths" — the deepest interior of the infernal realm from which evil ascends.

The spiritual reading says "fixed and rooted in the perverted perceptions arrayed against wisdom"; "that were arrayed" describes the trees (perverted perceptions) set in battle order against the Light.
The conjunction "and" connects the two phases of evil's self-generation: "it generated itself and it formed the fruits" — generation of perverted perceptions followed by formation of evil works.
The spiritual reading says "drew sustaining power"; "drew strength from the elements" describes the derivative evils absorbing power from the fundamental infernal qualities.

The spiritual reading transitions to "Wickedness together with cruelty concentrated"; "And all the" introduces the comprehensive gathering — all the wickedness together with cruelty gathered in the ruler, paralleling the next sentence's "he gathered them all into him."

The spiritual reading says "concentrated in the ruling love of self"; "gathered" is the Kephalaia's verb for concentration — all wickedness and cruelty gathered in the ruler, paralleling "he gathered them all into him" later.
The spiritual reading says "commission for combat"; in the Kephalaia, the First Man entrusts a "command" — a directive charge for battle — to his garments before engaging the enemy.

The spiritual reading says "everything that would befall them"; "would come upon" is the Kephalaia's natural-plane expression for what will befall or happen to the divine principles in the coming combat.

The spiritual reading says "in proper order"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, the First Man arranged his garments "upon himself" — assuming the divine truths onto his own person in preparation for battle.
The spiritual reading says "against the coming danger"; the First Man draped his garments upon his limbs "against the coming danger" — preparing for the impending assault of evil.
The spiritual reading says "as evil rose against the elevated states"; "rose up against" describes the Darkness ascending in assault against the heights of the Light earth.
The fill completes "from the beginning" with the partially visible "inning"; the spiritual reading says "from the very beginning" — evil's assault extending from the primordial origin.
